chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah or others from whom he narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who buys something that spoils from its day, and leaves it until he brings the price, he said: 'If he brings the price between it and the night, [the sale is valid], otherwise there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ اللَّيْلِ: between it (the transaction/day) and the night

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling perishable goods if the buyer delays payment until night?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a time-bound condition for sales of perishable goods, reflecting the practical need to prevent loss (*darar*) in early Islamic commerce. The ruling, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Kazim, emphasizes that failure to pay by nightfall invalidates the transaction, thereby protecting the seller from spoilage and ensuring swift settlement in trade contracts.
